title: Testfile
description: Schema for a Testfile (Testfile, testfile.yaml or testfile.yml): a declarative description of how a project runs its tests. A Testfile describes a test suite: tests nest. Each test either runs a command or a script, or groups nested tests that run in sequence or in parallel. Any test can be expanded through a matrix. Tests can depend on services (local processes or containers) that are started before and gracefully stopped after the test. The format is currently version 0 and under review; version 1 is targeted for Q4 2026. Feedback is welcome via GitHub issues at https://github.com/christoph-jerolimov/testfile/issues.

version.description: Version of the Testfile format. Currently always 0: the format is under review and may still change. Version 1 is targeted for Q4 2026. Feedback is welcome via GitHub issues at https://github.com/christoph-jerolimov/testfile/issues.

name.description: Human readable name of this Testfile / project.

env.description: Environment variables available to every test and service in this file.

envFile.description: Dotenv file(s), relative to this Testfile, loaded for the whole run. Values are treated as secrets: they are masked in recorded logs and never written into run records. Explicit 'env' entries win over env file values.

forwardEnv.description: Host environment variables forwarded into the test environment, which is otherwise isolated from the host (only essentials like PATH and HOME pass through, and the runner provides CI=1 with color output forced). Each entry is a variable name or a pattern where * matches anything, e.g. "GITHUB_*" or just "*".

ports.description: Named ports. A value of "random" allocates a free port on startup; an integer pins a fixed port. Referenced anywhere via ${{ ports.NAME }} templates.

services.description: Services that are started before the root test runs and gracefully stopped afterwards (also on Ctrl+C).

test.description: The root test of the suite.

envMap.description: Map of environment variable names to values. Non-string values are coerced to strings. Values may contain ${{ ... }} templates.

oneOf.description: Allocate a free port when the run starts.

duration.description: A duration, either as an integer number of seconds or as a string with a unit (ms, s, m, h), e.g. 30, "30s", "5m", "500ms".

matrix.description: Expands the test into one instance per combination of the given variables (cross product). Variables are available as ${{ matrix.NAME }} and as environment variables. The reserved keys 'exclude' and 'include' remove or add specific combinations.

exclude.description: Combinations to remove from the cross product. Each entry matches combinations that contain all of the given variable values.

include.description: Extra combinations to add after the cross product (and after 'exclude') has been evaluated.

test.description: A single test of the suite. Exactly one of 'command', 'script', 'sequence', 'parallel' or 'include' must be set.

name.description: Display name of this test. Matrix instances get the matrix values appended.

if.description: Condition deciding whether this test (and its nested tests) runs. Supports templates, truthiness ("", "false", "0", "no", "off" are false), "a == b" / "a != b" string comparison, and a leading "!" negating the whole expression. Unknown template references resolve to "". A false condition marks the test as skipped without failing the parent. Example: "${{ env.CI }}" or "${{ env.TESTFILE_OS }} == linux".

tags.description: Optional labels (letters and digits only) to group tests, e.g. fast, slow, flaky, nightly, aws, gcp. A tag applies to the test and all its nested tests; runners can filter by tag to execute a subset of tests.

env.description: Environment variables for this test and its children. Merged over the parent environment.

envFile.description: Dotenv file(s), relative to this test's working directory, loaded for this test and its nested tests. Values are treated as secrets: masked in recorded logs and never written into run records. Precedence: parent env < env file(s) < this test's 'env'.

forwardEnv.description: Host environment variables forwarded into this test's (and its children's) environment, e.g. "GITHUB_*" or "*". Precedence: parent env < forwarded < env file(s) < this test's 'env'.

workdir.description: Working directory for this test and its children, relative to the Testfile location (or absolute).

timeout.description: Maximum time this test (including children) may run before it is aborted and reported as failed.

continueOnError.description: If true, a failure of this test does not abort the surrounding sequence and does not fail the parent (the failure is still reported).

retry.description: Retry a failing command/script test. A plain integer is the number of additional attempts; the object form adds a delay between attempts.

count.description: Number of additional attempts after the first failure.

services.description: Services scoped to this test and its nested tests: started before this test runs, gracefully stopped when it finishes.

inputs.description: Glob patterns (relative to the test's working directory) of the files this test depends on. When neither the matched files' content nor the test's configuration changed since the last passing run, runners may skip the test and reuse that result. Only on command/script tests.

artifacts.description: Glob patterns (relative to the test's working directory) of files the test produces, e.g. coverage reports or screenshots. The runner copies matching files into the recorded run's folder after the test finished - also when it failed.

setup.description: Runs after this test's services are ready and before its body. If setup fails, the body is skipped and the test fails (teardown still runs).

teardown.description: Always runs after this test's body - on success, failure and abort - before the test's services are stopped. A failing teardown fails an otherwise passing test.

command.description: A single shell command to run. The test passes when the command exits with code 0.

script.description: A multi-line shell script to run (executed with 'sh -e'). The test passes when the script exits with code 0.

shell.description: Interpreter for this test's command/script instead of sh, e.g. "bash", "bash -e" or "python3". Split on whitespace and invoked as <shell...> -c <source>, so the interpreter must support -c. Note that the default 'sh -e' behavior for scripts does not apply - add flags like -e yourself.

sequence.description: Child tests that run one after another. The sequence stops at the first failure unless that child sets continueOnError.

parallel.description: Child tests that run at the same time. The group fails if any child fails.

include.description: Path or glob (relative to this Testfile) of another Testfile - or a directory containing one - to embed here. The included file's env and services are scoped to the embedded tests, its ports merge into this file's ports, and its tests run with the included file's directory as working directory. A glob matching several files embeds them as a parallel group. Not templated; 'workdir' cannot be combined with include.

maxParallel.description: Maximum number of children of 'parallel' running at the same time. Defaults to unlimited.

needs.description: Only on children of a 'parallel' group: names of sibling tests that must finish first. The test starts once all named siblings passed (or were skipped); if one failed, this test is skipped. References must be unambiguous and cycle-free.

retry.description: retry only applies to command/script tests, not to groups.

inputs.description: inputs only applies to command/script tests, not to groups.

shell.description: shell only applies to command/script tests, not to groups.

hook.description: A command or script that runs around a test. Exactly one of 'command' or 'script' must be set.

service.description: A long-running dependency (web server, database, ...) needed by tests. Exactly one of 'command', 'script' or 'container' must be set. The runner waits for the 'ready' check before starting the dependent tests and stops the service gracefully afterwards.

shared.description: Share one running instance between tests whose resolved service configuration is identical - e.g. matrix instances that do not vary this service. The service starts with the first test that needs it and stops after the last one finished. Configurations that differ (e.g. a matrix variable in the image) still get their own instance.

needs.description: Names of services in the same map that must be ready before this one starts (docker-compose's depends_on, but always gated on the readiness check). Cycles and unknown names are rejected.

command.description: Start the service as a local process running this shell command.

script.description: Start the service as a local process running this shell script (executed with 'sh -e').

container.description: Run the service as a container image.

image.description: The container image to run, e.g. docker.io/library/postgres:16.

engine.description: Container engine to use. 'auto' picks podman if available, otherwise docker. 'kubernetes' (local or remote cluster) is reserved for a future version.

ports.description: Port mappings as "HOST:CONTAINER". The host part may be a template, e.g. "${{ ports.db }}:5432".

pull.description: When to pull the image: always, only when missing locally (default), or never.

network.description: Attach the container to this named network, creating it if needed. The service name becomes a network alias, so services on the same network reach each other by name.

ready.description: How the runner detects that a service is ready. At least one of 'http', 'tcp', 'log' or 'exec' must be set. Checks are polled until they succeed or 'timeout' is reached.

http.description: Ready when an HTTP request succeeds. A plain string is a URL expected to answer with a 2xx status.

status.description: Expected status code. Defaults to any 2xx.

tcp.description: Ready when a TCP connection can be established. A plain value is a port on localhost; the port may be a template string.

exec.description: Ready when this shell command exits with code 0, e.g. pg_isready or redis-cli ping. Runs in the service's environment and working directory.

log.description: Ready when the service output matches this regular expression. A plain string matches on any stream.

delay.description: Wait this long before the first check.

timeout.description: Give up (and fail the run) when the service is not ready after this time. Defaults to 30s.

stop.description: How the service is stopped. By default the runner sends 'signal' (SIGTERM) and escalates to SIGKILL after 'timeout'. Containers are stopped with their engine's stop command using the same timeout.

command.description: Run this shell command to stop the service instead of sending a signal.
